title: Direction & Wrapping 🔀
description: Control the flow with `flex-direction`, `flex-wrap`, and the `flex-flow` shorthand.

slides.title: `flex-direction`: Setting the Main Axis 🧭
Direction Examples
slides.codeSnippet:
.row { flex-direction: row; }           /* [1] [2] [3] */
.row-reverse { flex-direction: row-reverse; } /* [3] [2] [1] */
.column { flex-direction: column; }      /* items stacked vertically */

quizData.question: With `flex-direction: column;`, which axis is the main axis?
quizData.explanation: `column` makes the main axis vertical, so items stack top to bottom.

slides.title: `flex-wrap`: When Items Overflow 📦
slides.content:
# Allow Wrapping to Next Line/Column

By default, flex items try to fit on one line (`nowrap`). If they exceed the container, they shrink or overflow. `flex-wrap` changes that:
- `nowrap` (default) – single line, items may shrink.
- `wrap` – items wrap onto multiple lines (or columns).
- `wrap-reverse` – wraps in reverse order.

```css
.container {
  flex-wrap: wrap;
}
```
Wrapping works along the cross axis: in a row layout, items wrap onto new rows below.

slides.title: The `flex-flow` Shorthand 🩳

quizData.question: What does `flex-flow: column wrap;` do?

options.text: Items stack in a column and wrap into new columns
Items stack in a row and wrap into new rows

quizData.explanation: `column wrap` creates a vertical main axis and allows wrapping into additional columns.
